A_target.statement:
There exists a [[Definition:Countably Additive Function|countably additive]] [[Definition:Measure (Measure Theory)|measure]] $\lambda$ on the [[Definition:Lebesgue Sigma-Algebra|Lebesgue $\sigma$-algebra]] $\mathcal L$ of $\R$ such that:
:$\map \lambda {\closedint a b} = b - a$
for every [[Definition:Closed Real Interval|closed interval]].

B_source.statement:
Let $a, b \in \R$ with $a \le b$.
The [[Definition:Length of Real Interval|length]] of $\closedint a b$ is:
:$\map \ell {\closedint a b} = b - a$

substitutions.the length of an interval: the outer measure, an infimum over countable interval covers
substitutions.finite additivity for adjacent intervals: countable additivity for disjoint measurable sets

derived.the covering definition: outer measure, defined for every subset
derived.the restriction to well-behaved sets: the Caratheodory criterion, selecting the measurable sets

object_map.reformulation: Extend length from intervals to arbitrary sets by covering, then cut back to the sets where additivity survives.

validity_conditions: Outer measure is defined for every subset by covering with intervals, but it is only countably subadditive in general, not additive.
Restricting to sets satisfying the Caratheodory splitting criterion yields a sigma-algebra on which the measure is countably additive.
Some restriction is unavoidable: assuming choice, no countably additive translation-invariant measure assigns a size to every subset of the line.
proof_plan:
Define the [[Definition:Lebesgue Outer Measure|outer measure]]:
:$\displaystyle \map {\lambda^*} A = \inf \set {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty \map \ell {I_k}: A \subseteq \bigcup_{k \mathop = 1}^\infty I_k}$
the infimum over countable covers by intervals.

Covering $\closedint a b$ by itself gives $\map {\lambda^*} {\closedint a b} \le b - a$.
By the [[Heine-Borel Theorem]], any cover has a finite subcover whose total length is at least $b - a$.
Hence $\lambda^*$ agrees with $\ell$ on intervals.

Let $\mathcal L$ be the sets $E$ satisfying the [[Definition:Carathéodory's Criterion|Carathéodory criterion]]:
:$\forall A \subseteq \R: \map {\lambda^*} A = \map {\lambda^*} {A \cap E} + \map {\lambda^*} {A \setminus E}$
By [[Carathéodory's Theorem (Measure Theory)|Carathéodory's Theorem]], $\mathcal L$ is a [[Definition:Sigma-Algebra|$\sigma$-algebra]] containing the intervals.

By the same theorem, $\lambda = \lambda^* \restriction_{\mathcal L}$ is [[Definition:Countably Additive Function|countably additive]] on $\mathcal L$.
{{qed}}
